Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 2:41: And so they said, of blessed memory, in the Mechilta (Parashat Mishpatim), on the verse (Exodus 22:30), "and you shall be holy men to Me" - Rabbi Yishmael says, when you are holy, you are Mine - to this point. He comes to explain the word "to Me," which is superfluous, and says that the verse explains: when you are holy men, "you are Mine" - meaning, we have a relation to be bound as one, as Scripture says (Leviticus 19:2), "you shall be holy, for I am holy," and as we elaborated above, in the previous chapter, that Israel must be a suitable vessel to receive His holiness. And from the affirmative you infer the negative - that if one is not sanctified, he is not His - for what relation does a physical man have to be bound with the spiritual and holy One, possessor of all holinesses, may He be exalted and blessed, if he does not sanctify himself and separate from the affairs of the world? He is found to be physical, dominated by mere doing [Asiyah], and behold he is "other" and not His - for whatever a person sanctifies, even if it be a small measure of holiness in the secret of the nefesh, it becomes His, blessed be He, in one secret, as will be explained, with God's help; but if not, he is "other." Therefore let the living take it to heart, to sanctify himself and cleave to Him, blessed be He, as much as he can.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:1: After explaining, in the previous chapter, that a person is obligated to sanctify each and every day of the six days of the week and conduct himself in it with the holiness of the day of Shabbat, it is fitting to explain what the holinesses are that one must observe on the day of Shabbat and the other days.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:2: And we say that although the holinesses are many, as found in the Torah and the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, as will be explained, what is found written concerning the day of Shabbat are three: the first, the holiness of thought; the second, the holiness of speech; the third, the holiness of labor - and these three are the essential means for a person to cleave.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:3: And although eating is permitted on Shabbat, this does not undermine the sanctification of the six weekdays - for even though a person eats on the six weekdays, if his eating is for the sake of Heaven, as will be explained, his eating will bring him to sanctify himself and cleave. Nevertheless, the eating of Shabbat is not like the eating of the weekdays, for in the eating of Shabbat, "delight" [oneg] is mentioned, as it is written (Isaiah 58:13), "and call the Sabbath a delight" - and this is the secret of "*Eden," "*nahar" [river], "*gan" [garden] [together spelling ONeG], as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:4: And so concerning marital relations on Shabbat night, which they elaborated on in the Zohar (Parashat Yitro, page 89a), saying that of this it is said, "you shall be holy" - and even if another person learns from the marital relations found on Shabbat and applies it to the weekdays, if he sanctifies himself on weekdays at midnight, as will be explained, in the manner of the union of Shabbat night, he has not lost anything.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:5: The holiness of thought we find concerning Shabbat in the Mechilta (Parashat Yitro), in these words: "six days you shall labor" (Exodus 20:9) - and is it possible for a person to do all his work in six days? Rather, rest as though all your work were done. Another interpretation: rest from thoughts of labor - to this point. Behold, it is explicit that we are warned not to think of any matter of worldly affairs, so that our thought be cleaved to the Name, blessed be He, and to everything that is His service.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:6: And so concerning the holiness of speech, as Scripture says (Isaiah 58:13), "from pursuing your business, and speaking words [of idle talk]" - and they elaborated at length in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel, page 205b), concerning one who speaks weekday talk on Shabbat, that he is like one who desecrates Shabbat, as we shall further elaborate below (chapter 14).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:7: The holiness of labor is explained in several verses in the Torah (Exodus 35:2), "six days work shall be done, but on the seventh day there shall be a holy day for you, a Sabbath of rest to the LORD," and likewise in the Ten Commandments (ibid. 20:9), "six days you shall labor and do [all your work], but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God." And in saying "to the LORD your God," you should think as though all your work were done, and you have nothing of the affairs of this world - so that the whole day be holy and you cleave to the LORD your God. And this is "Shabbat Shabbaton" - "Shabbat" in deed, "Shabbaton, kodesh" in thought.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:8: And you already know that "kodesh" is in the secret of thought, and therefore a person is obligated to sanctify his thought on the day of Shabbat and separate it from all matters of the physicality of this world - for the whole reality of Shabbat is holy, and it is the secret of the world of souls that opens on Shabbat, as they said in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 136a), that souls in the lower Garden of Eden ascend to the upper Garden of Eden, and supernal souls descend to crown Israel; and likewise souls refined during the six weekdays enter the lower Garden of Eden - and he says, on the eve of Shabbat, the reincarnation cycles of souls (according to what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, taught us, and so on, as mentioned above) occurs: these go and those come, these descend - who sees how many holy chariots roam here and there, all in joy, all encircling these souls to crown the holy people, to crown several righteous ones in the lower Garden of Eden - until the hour the herald stands and calls, "sanctified, sanctified," then there is rest, a stilling of all, and the wicked of Gehinnom are all stilled and have rest, and all the souls are crowned in their places, these above and these below - happy is the people whose portion is this - to this point. And so he further says on (page 72), and every Shabbat eve a person sits in the world of souls. And so he says in the Zohar (Parashat Emor, page 95a), on this day of Shabbat all pain, anger, and distress from the whole world are forgotten, because it is the day of the King's wedding feast, when souls are added, in the manner of the World to Come - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:9: And since the day of Shabbat is holy because souls are added to it, it is fitting to make it a priority for the added soul to sanctify itself with its supernal holiness in every kind of holiness - and the holiness of thought is above all of them, for it is the secret of the additional soul added from above, from the place of holiness, as explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Tzav, page 29a; Parashat Pinchas, pages 242b and 243a) - meaning that there is an addition of soul from the Cause of causes, but for each one according to his aspect: there is an addition of nefesh from several aspects, and there is an addition of ru'ach and an addition of neshamah - see there. And therefore the essential thing that the additional soul enjoys is from the intention of prayer and novel insights of Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:10: And so it is fitting for another reason - for "the tabernacle of peace spreads its wings over us," as explained in Parashat Bereshit (Zohar, page 48a), and Scripture says (Numbers 28:10), "the burnt offering of every Sabbath in its Sabbath, besides the continual burnt offering" - meaning that its ascent every single Shabbat is more than what ascends continually every day of the six days of the week, and this is "besides the continual burnt offering." And therefore, according to its refinement and ascent, greater refinement of thought and inner intention is needed than on the other days.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:11: And concerning novel insights of Torah, they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Shelach Lecha, page 173a), in these words: come and see, when Shabbat enters, souls descend and rest upon the holy people, and the souls of the righteous ascend above; when Shabbat departs, the souls that rested upon Israel ascend, and the souls that descend are the souls of the righteous. Once all the souls that rested upon Israel ascend, they stand in form before the holy King - the Holy One, blessed be He, asks all of them, what novel Torah insight did this soul of so-and-so say? And they all establish that matter in the two academies, those below, and the Holy One, blessed be He, above seals that matter. Come and see, when a matter is renewed in Torah, and the soul that descended on Shabbat is occupied with those new matters and ascends above, all the retinue above listens to that matter, and the Holy Chayot grow in their wings and are clothed in wings - and when the Holy One, blessed be He, asks and they do not know, and are silent, then the Holy Chayot - what is written (Ezekiel 1:24)? "When they stood, they let down their wings" - along the lines of (Job 32:16), "when they stood still and answered no more," and "and as he opened it, all the people stood up" (Nehemiah 8:5).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:12: Further, they said in Midrash Yalkut (Psalm 139, section 888, page 129d), on the verse "my unformed substance [golmi]": Rabbi Yehoshua says, they are 365, and the unification of the world is one of them. Rabbi Levi said, this is the Day of Atonement - "is such the fast that I have chosen, a day for a man to afflict his soul" (Isaiah 58:5). Rabbi Yitzchak said, this is the day of Shabbat, as it is said (Exodus 20:8), "remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy" - how does a person do it? He labors all six days and rests on the seventh, reconciling with his children and household - and even though you labor all six days, the day of Shabbat should be entirely Torah. From here they said, a person should rise early and sit on the day of Shabbat and go to the synagogue and the study hall, and read from the Torah and study the Prophets, and afterward go home and eat and drink, to fulfill what is said (Ecclesiastes 9:7), "go, eat your bread with joy" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:13: Further, in Tanna D'Vei Eliyahu, Yalkut Parashat Va'etchanan (section 830, page 265), in explanation of the verse, in these words: "remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy" - with what do you sanctify it? With Scripture reading, with numbering [of the days], with food and drink, and with clean clothing - and although Rabbi Akiva said, make your Sabbath like a weekday and do not depend on others, one should still take meat and not overindulge in wine, as it is said (Proverbs 23:20), "be not among winebibbers" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:14: And having explained the holiness of Shabbat in a general way, it is fitting that, every single day, one flow into it from that holiness, each according to his ability, whether for part of the day, most of it, or sometimes all of it - namely, that he cease from his labor and seclude himself to occupy himself with Torah, and clear his thought from worldly affairs - for it is not fitting for a person to occupy himself with labor all day, as they said in the Zohar (Parashat Beshalach, page 63a), along these lines: those who do not believe in the Holy One, blessed be He, do not wish to gaze at His ways, and they wish to trouble themselves every day after sustenance, day and night, lest a morsel of bread not come into their hand - who causes this to them? Because they are not people of faith - to this point. And therefore it is fitting for a person to make his Torah fixed and his labor occasional, as they said in Tractate Avot (chapter 4, mishnah 10): Rabbi Meir says, minimize your business and occupy yourself with Torah, and if you neglect Torah, you will have many neglects [i.e., excuses], and so on. And this is not specific to Torah, but to every matter of a commandment, acts of kindness, and the like - Rabbenu Tam wrote in Sefer HaYashar (the second gate, the sixth measure), concerning the matter of love, that one of the signs of love is not to let any of his own affairs precede the affairs of God, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:15: Further, they said in Midrash Rut (Midrash Zuta 1:20) that a certain pious man was very poor, and Elijah appeared to him in the guise of an Arab, and gave him two coins, and he traded with them and became rich, and through his trading and business he forgot the timing of his piety and the performance of his prayer. Elijah returned to him and took back the two coins he had given him, and he lost his possessions and that money went to waste. The pious man returned to weeping, and so on; Elijah returned to him and said, I swear that if I return those two coins to you, will you keep the timing of your piety and the performance of your prayer? He said to him, yes - and he took the two coins and traded with them and became rich. Behold, that a person should not abandon the timing of his piety for the sake of business dealings - and the reason is as explained, that one is obligated to make holy out of the profane.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:16: And in the Mechilta (Parashat Ki Tisa), they said, of blessed memory: "six days shall work be done" (Exodus 35:2) - passive voice - and one verse says (ibid. 20:9), "six days you shall labor and do all your work" - active voice - how can these two verses be reconciled? Rather, when Israel does the will of the Omnipresent, their work is done by others, as it is said "shall work be done," and so it says (Isaiah 61:5), "and strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and foreigners shall be your plowmen and vinedressers"; and when they do not do the will of the Omnipresent, their work is done by themselves, as it is said, "and do all your work" - and not only that, but "and you shall serve your enemies whom the LORD shall send against you" (Deuteronomy 28:48) - to this point. And along these lines they brought there, in Parashat Vayakhel, on the verse (Exodus 35:2), "six days shall work be done." Behold, that man was not created to be occupied with physical labors that keep him from Torah study, but rather that all his days be like Shabbat, occupied with Torah, and that strangers stand to do his labor - and this at a time when Israel does the will of the Omnipresent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:17: And one must be precise here, for we find several pious men in the Gemara who were occupied with their labor and occupied with Torah, such as Hillel and his companions - why was their labor not done by others? One could resolve this with some difficulty, that the discourse spoke only in general terms, "at a time when Israel does the will of the Omnipresent," and so on - but the question remains, why does not every fit person merit this?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:18: And one may say that there are two other aspects to this, besides what is said in the first discourse - for we already find, among the earlier pious ones, an example of this matter, as they said in Tractate Berachot (chapter 5, mishnah 1), that the early pious ones would take an hour before prayer and an hour after prayer and an hour during prayer - that is three hours - and so for each prayer, Shacharit, Mincha, and Ma'ariv - and they asked in the Gemara (32b, and cf. Yerushalmi, chapter 5, halachah 1), when was their Torah study and their labor done? And they answered, since they are pious, their Torah is blessed and their labor is done of itself - it follows that of these too it is said, "work shall be done" - meaning, they begin a small part of the labor, and blessing and success are found in that labor. But it is not quite the same as when all of Israel does the will of the Omnipresent, for the merit of the many is preferable, and all their labor is done by others; but when they do not do the will of the Omnipresent, "and do all your work" - meaning through himself he shall do all his work.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:19: And the second aspect, which is not quite like the early pious ones, is the matter of the Tannaim and Amoraim, who occupied themselves part of the day with their labor - however, their labor was done through their outer, visible limbs, while their thought and soul were cleaved to the LORD, blessed be He, and to His Torah. And do not find this difficult, for it is written in the book Ma'aseh HaChassidim, found in manuscript, that a certain pious man was a recluse among those secluded ones separated from worldly affairs, always cleaved to the LORD, blessed be He, and in the course of time this pious man came to a settlement and was not recognized, and they made him the synagogue's sexton - and when he would put oil in the candles, he would spill some of the oil outside, for from the abundance of his cleaving he could not focus on putting the oil inside the candles. And the community's sage understood the matter and said, this sexton deserves to be the sage in my place, and I shall serve under him - and concerning something like this it is said (Proverbs 5:19), "in her love you shall always be lost" - for from the abundance of love of Torah and cleaving to it, he becomes lost regarding the matters of this world. It follows that if their souls were always sanctified with the holiness of Shabbat, which is the world of thought, as explained above [they could do this]. But when it is not fitting, and one does not occupy himself with Torah, his whole body and soul are enslaved to labor.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:20: And in our time, when Torah scholars do not occupy themselves with labor, and are supported by the wealthy of the generation, they have something to rely on, namely what is said in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Tzav, page 29a), that Torah scholars, called "sons," serve on condition of not receiving reward - that on weekdays they have the soul of Atzilut, which the rest of the people, who serve on condition of receiving reward, merit only on the day of Shabbat, for on weekdays they have only the spirit of Metatron. And these Torah scholars are called "Shabbat" even on weekdays, for they have no labor except the yoke of Torah and commandments; upon the common people falls the obligation to sustain and support them. And he says, whoever does not occupy himself with Torah and commandments has upon him the yoke of the kingdom of the gentiles; whoever occupies himself with Torah and commandments has upon him the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven, which is the final heh, called the kingdom of Heaven - certainly the yoke of a kingdom, for through her all the creatures of heaven and earth were created, this is what is written (Genesis 2:4), "these are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created [be-hibar'am]" - with a heh He created them; and when Shabbatot and festivals come, Binah, which is Yah, descends upon the heh, which is the kingdom of Heaven - an additional soul - and this is [the inscription] engraved on the tablets, "I am [He] of the exodus from Egypt," and the spreading of her wings over her daughter and her camps, and they have rest. And he further says on, that Torah scholars have nothing of their own, and if an ignorant person supports him with his money and treats him according to his will, to serve, to be conducted in the commandments according to his will, "man and beast You save, O LORD" is fulfilled in him - He saves him from plunder and robbery, He saves him from the attribute of judgment, which does not rule over him, and slaughters him with an invalid knife, of which it is said (Exodus 22:30), "you shall cast it to the dogs" - this is Samael. And the soul of a Torah scholar is called "Shabbat, the queen, the additional soul," and so on. And he further says on, that these Torah scholars are the sons of the King and the Matronita, called Shabbatot and festivals, and have nothing of their own, for they are not laborers like other servants, the sons of the profane; their reward, in this world and the World to Come, is to be delighted with every kind of food and drink, and to be honored with fine garments, along the lines of Shabbat, of which it is said, "honor it with clean clothing" - whatever a person does for Shabbatot and festivals, he must do for them, and whoever desecrates them is liable for stoning; so too whoever makes use of a crown is exchanged [punished], and so too one who makes use of one who studies halachot desecrates his Torah - and all the more so one who disgraces him, as though he disgraces Shabbatot and festivals - and the masters of the Mishnah established, whoever disgraces the festivals is as though he denies the fundamental principle. And along the lines that all the vessels of the Temple are called holy, so all those who serve Torah scholars are called holy, and the students of a master, who correspond to the limbs of his body, are called "holy of holies" - and the secret of the matter is alluded to in them (Exodus 26:33), "and the veil shall divide for you between the holy and the holy of holies" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:21: Behold, that a Torah scholar whose profession is Torah, and does not occupy himself with labor, and has nothing to support himself with, is permitted to benefit [from others' support] - for he is a holy Shabbat, sanctified on the weekdays with the holiness of Shabbat. And such a Torah scholar, who does not occupy himself with labor at all, must, without doubt, sanctify his speech on weekdays as his speech on Shabbat, and likewise sanctify his thought, as explained above, and the other holinesses to be explained, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:22: And for this reason, Rashbi, peace be upon him, who sanctified himself on weekdays with all the holiness of the day of Shabbat, was called "Shabbat" by his companions - in these words, at the end of the Idra of Naso (page 144b): Rabbi Abba said, we are the six lamps that shine from the seventh; you are the seventh of all, for the six have no existence except through the seventh, for everything depends on the seventh. Rabbi Yehuda calls him "the Shabbat of all six," as it is written, "a Sabbath to the LORD," "holy to the LORD" - just as "a Sabbath to the LORD" is holy, so Rabbi Shimon is "a Sabbath to the LORD, holy" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 3:23: And if he is occupied with labor, he must sanctify part of the day from being occupied with labor, and likewise sanctify his thought, his speech, and his other senses, as will be explained, with God's help - and at least at the time of prayer, when he is necessarily free of labor, he shall sanctify his thought from worldly affairs, so that that hour, or half hour, be holy with the holiness of Shabbat, and not interrupt his prayer with speech at all - in such a way that no day be entirely devoid of the holiness of Shabbat.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:1: Since our discourse preceded, in the previous chapter, that the holiness of Shabbat is comprised of three things - thought, speech, deed - we saw fit to follow it with this chapter, to explain what is found, in allusion to this matter, in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, and the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:2: The three things mentioned in holiness, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (end of Tikkun 22, page 68b), are neshamah, ru'ach, nefesh - thought corresponding to the neshamah, speech corresponding to the ru'ach, deed corresponding to the nefesh. In these words: the four foundations of the body, in which YHVH rests, and this is "everyone who is called by My name, and whom I have created for My glory, I have formed him, yes, I have made him" (Isaiah 43:7) - "I have created him" - this is the holy soul [neshamah], which is the world of thought; "I have formed him" - this is the speaking spirit [ru'ach] from which the speaking creatures [Chayot] speak; "I have made him" - this is the nefesh, where deed [asiyah] rests, in the 248 commandments - to this point. It follows that His intent, blessed be He, is to sanctify us with the three holinesses mentioned, so that we sanctify our nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah from the holiness of Atzilut flowing in all the worlds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:3: And this is "sanctify yourselves," and so on, "for I the LORD am your God" (Leviticus 20:7), and likewise "you shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy" (Leviticus 19:2) - and these three words, "ani YHVH Eloheichem" [I the LORD your God], correspond to nefesh, ru'ach, neshamah - and the intent is that from Him, blessed be He, comes the flow of the nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah, and all three of these aspects are holinesses through which they cleave to Him and He to them. And the reason he says, in the appellation corresponding to the neshamah, "Eloheichem" [your God], is that there is no cleaving of a person to God, blessed be He, except through the neshamah, which is from the world of thought - and when he merits the supernal neshamah, then he is cleaved to his Creator, then the Holy One, blessed be He, is appellated as his God, and the Shechinah rests upon him - and along this path it is correct in all the places mentioned in Parashat Kedoshim, "ani YHVH Eloheichem" - the intent being that the three attributes mentioned, which comprise all ten, dwell upon the soul that repairs the commandments - and therefore, at the beginning of Parashat Kedoshim, it says "you shall be holy, for I am holy" - meaning, just as I am holy, so shall you be holy - and the intent is concerning the sanctification of the person himself, in nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah, through the commandments and Torah and the repair of his thoughts and intentions - and through this, "ani YHVH Eloheichem," meaning the attributes mentioned dwell within you - and this is what was explained in the first chapter, that souls must be a suitable vessel to receive His holiness, as explained in the Tanchuma discourse at the beginning of the chapter (chapter 1).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:4: And these three flow into Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah, as will be further explained below, with God's help - and corresponding to these three worlds, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah, is what the Torah commanded, "sanctify yourselves and be holy, for I am holy" - and so they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Balak, page 190b), in these words: the supernal praise that is not given over to the supernal angels alone, but to Israel - what is it? Holiness. Blessing is given over to them alone, as it is given to Israel; but holiness is not given over to them alone, only together with Israel, for they do not sanctify holiness except together with Israel. And should you say, but it is written (Isaiah 6:3), "and one called to another, and said" [implying the angels alone say the Kedushah] - when? At the time Israel sanctifies below; and until Israel sanctifies below, they do not say the Kedushah - because holiness ascends from three worlds and not from two - and this is "and called" - this is one; "to another" - two; "and said" - behold, three. Three worlds correspond to three holinesses - and therefore the praise of Israel is that they take holiness below. Rabbi Elazar said, so it is, and we have established these words, and further we have established that three holinesses are given over to Israel below, from this verse (Leviticus 20:7), "sanctify yourselves and be holy, for I am holy" - "sanctify yourselves" - one; "and be holy" - two; "for I am holy" - behold, three. Here are three holinesses - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:5: And one is compelled to say that these three holinesses are in the mentioned places, because above this it says that Israel took deed [Asiyah] below from the time of the giving of the Torah onward, when they said "we shall do and we shall hear" - and this is "mighty in strength, who do His word" (Psalms 103:20), and so on - and therefore holiness ascends only from three worlds, namely with Israel's participation, who are in Asiyah below, together with the angels, who are in Yetzirah - and this is "one to another"; "and said" - everything ascends and is elevated and bound with Beriah, "holy, holy, holy," which is in Atzilut. And this is "sanctify yourselves," and this is "I the LORD" - for "holy" is in Beriah, "I the LORD" is in Atzilut - the primary Beings, He and His life being one within them, from which flows all the holinesses, as explained - and this is "ani YHVH Eloheichem."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:6: And should you say, why are only three holinesses mentioned, and not a fourth holiness corresponding to Atzilut? One may say that Atzilut, because of its subtlety and concealment, being the secret of concealed thought, we have no power to make ourselves a chariot for it - and behold, even Beriah is thought, all the more so Atzilut. And because Beriah is thought, the verse does not mention, concerning it, an action of preparing holiness within us, as it mentioned in the two preceding, "sanctify yourselves and be holy" - but concerning the third it says "for I am holy" - of Myself I am holy. And since the lower throne, from Asiyah and Yetzirah, is prepared - these corresponding to nefesh and ru'ach - the holiness of the neshamah, which is thought, rests of itself, and Atzilut is unified within Beriah - for Rashbi, peace be upon him, called Beriah, in the Tikkunim (page 3b), "the garments of Shabbat and festivals" - for it is impossible for the light of Atzilut, because of its concealment, to be revealed to us except through Beriah - and therefore, between Beriah and Atzilut, Scripture does not mention a fourth holiness, but rather "holy" in Beriah, "I the LORD," which is Atzilut clothed within it, and it is all one unity.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:7: We find we learn that it is impossible for a person to sanctify his thought to be cleaved to the Name, blessed be He, except through the neshamah that comes to him from the world of thought, as explained above - and the neshamah rests only if its throne, which is nefesh and ru'ach, are repaired. And for this he must repair his soul with the complete fulfillment of the commandments, and sanctify himself from performing labor, which is in Asiyah, and sanctify all the vessels of his limbs, in which is deed; and afterward sanctify corresponding to ru'ach; and when this is repaired, the supernal neshamah rests upon him, and behold he is holy, cleaved to Him, blessed be He. And nevertheless, the neshamah does not rest of itself except through acquiring it by one's deeds and Torah, as explained at the beginning of Parashat Mishpatim (page 94b), which says, whoever merits more is given a soul from the side of the throne. However, even if he makes preparations to acquire them, the neshamah will not rest in him if its throne, which are nefesh and ru'ach, are not properly repaired.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:8: And in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra, page 25a), they explained that whoever merits the neshamah, his soul ascends above every night into the world of souls, and he is cleaved and bound in the bond of life more than one who has merited only the ru'ach - for in acquiring the ru'ach, one ascends only to the world of angels. In these words: once he has acquired ru'ach, that ru'ach goes forth, breaking through mountains and cliffs, ascends and spreads and enters among the supernal holy angels, and there knows what it knows and learns matters, and returns to its place - then this is the bond of a person with holiness, until he merits the neshamah and acquires it. Once he has acquired the neshamah, it ascends higher and higher, and the guardians of the gates do not delay it, and it goes and spreads among those righteous ones bound in the bond of life, and there it sees the delight of the King and delights in the supernal splendor - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:9: Further, we find a necessity for the reality of these three holinesses in the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, in Yoma (39a), in these words: our Rabbis taught, "sanctify yourselves and be holy" (Leviticus 11:44) - if a person sanctifies himself a little, they sanctify him much; if from below, they sanctify him from above; in this world, they sanctify him for the World to Come - to this point. And before this, adjacent to it, they said there, in these words: our Rabbis taught, "do not defile yourselves with them" (Leviticus 11:43) - if a person defiles himself a little, they defile him much; if from below, they defile him from above; in this world, they defile him for the World to Come - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:10: And behold, based on the introduction we gave concerning the matter of the mentioned holinesses, it is possible to say that the author of the discourse intended this, in the matter of the three divisions - "sanctifies himself a little," "from below," "in this world" - which correspond to Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah, from below upward. And it is explained by what is explained in the Tikkunim (beginning of page 23a), that the supernal Mother nests in the throne, in the three supernal sefirot; the middle pillar, comprising six sefirot, nests in Metatron; the lower Mother nests in the "ofan" [wheel], of which it is said, "and behold one wheel upon the earth" - to this point. And the intent is that according to how a person sanctifies himself in the lower levels, holiness flows into him from the supernal levels in Atzilut - and this is "for I the LORD your God am holy," as explained above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:11: How so? "He sanctifies himself a little" - namely, the holiness of Asiyah, which is the "ofan" - "they sanctify him much" - because the branch arouses the supernal root in Atzilut, and the Shechinah, who is "Ani" [I], nests in the "ofan," flowing there from her holiness, which is much in proportion to the small branch, which is the "ofan." And further, concerning the Shechinah, the matter of abundance [rov] is fitting, as it is said (Psalms 104:24), "how manifold [rabu] are Your works, O LORD; in wisdom You have made them all," and so on - meaning, through "mah" [what], which is the Shechinah, "Your works are manifold" [rabu]. And so, in the Heichal of Livnat HaSapir, which corresponds to the Shechinah, we say in the Yotzer Or blessing, "mah rabu ma'asecha Hashem" [how manifold are Your works, O LORD], as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Pekudei, page 260b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:12: "If from below, they sanctify him from above" - the intent is that in sanctifying himself further, in Metatron, who is below - and he called him with the appellation "below" as explained in the Tikkunim (page 4a) and the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 228b), that Metatron is the horse on which Tiferet rides, and just as the horse is below and the rider upon it is above, so is Metatron - and in these words (Ra'aya Meheimna, ibid.): Metatron is the horse of Tiferet, in which all the sefirot are clothed, and this is like a body to a soul - to this point. And "they sanctify him from above" means that Tiferet, which is YHVH, shall shine into Metatron like a soul in a body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:13: "In this world, they sanctify him for the World to Come" - this is the third holiness, in Beriah, called "this world," for everything below the Shechinah is called "this world," just as she herself is called "this world," along the lines of "be-hibar'am," "with a heh He created them" (Menachot 29b), for through the final heh was the creation of all the lower worlds. And "they sanctify him for the World to Come" is the illumination of the supernal Mother, called "Eloheichem" [your God], in the three supernal sefirot that nest in the throne. This is one way in this discourse, according to the introduction we gave.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:14: And concerning impurity, in which three levels are explained, they are also along this path - except that what he says, "they defile him much," "from above," "for the World to Come," the intent is that "they defile him" means the closing off of the flow, so that it not flow down into Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah - for the three levels mentioned in the discourse concerning impurity are on the verse (Leviticus 11:43), "and do not defile yourselves with them, and you become defiled by them" - and they expounded in Yoma (39b) that "u-nitmetem" [and you become defiled] is a term of "timtum" [dulling/stopping up] - and they said, of blessed memory: the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught, it dulls a person's heart, as it is said, "do not defile yourselves with them, and you become defiled by them" - do not read "u-nitmetem" but "u-nitamtem" [and you are dulled] - to this point.
